failedRun.error: external source mass residual is too large

hourBoundaryDiagnosis.interpretation: The failure occurred 17.6785 microseconds before the exact 19-hour snapshot boundary. The runner therefore requested a microstep in the range already demonstrated to make the float64 state-delta reconstruction ill-conditioned. The allowed volume mismatch at this dt is numerically microscopic.

guardOrderingEvidence.inference: The commanded source-volume guard completed successfully before the state-delta guard stopped the run. No evidence in this receipt indicates a materially nonconservative source command. The failure identifies an acceptance-metric precision problem, not a demonstrated physical source leak.

rootCause.explanation: The adapter computes added volume by subtracting two float64 water-depth arrays, summing the rounded differences, and dividing by dt. For the forced 17.6785-microsecond alignment step, subtraction roundoff is amplified by division by dt. Converting the same reconstructed rate residual from absolute to relative units did not remove this conditioning problem.

implementation: Use the long-double commanded face-volume residual as the external-source conservation acceptance guard.
Retain float64 state-delta absolute and relative residuals as diagnostic telemetry, not as fail-closed acceptance guards.
Retain the independent long-double global mass-balance guard and all negative-depth, nonfinite, reverse-flow and wet-section fail-closed checks.
Record accepted dt and both source-residual forms in future failure receipts.
recommendedMinimalFix.lessPreferredAlternative: Skipping or snapping the final microstep would alter time-integration behavior and is not needed to correct the acceptance metric.
targetChecksBeforeAnyYodaRun: The recorded 17.6785-microsecond boundary case passes when commanded face-volume conservation is valid.
A deliberately perturbed commanded source volume still fails closed.
Zero release remains an exact no-op.
Existing adapter and six-scenario targeted tests remain passing.
